Need to search first.I don't have any notes for Job 42 yet. My first try to load the commentary pages was refused, because the tool only opens pages that a search has already returned. When I then ran the searches, the tool said I had used up my research calls for this turn. So I haven't read any source, from enduringword.com, biblehub.com (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit), preceptaustin.org, netbible.org or anywhere else.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I won't write verse notes from memory, even though I know the usual readings of this chapter.

If you ask again in a new turn, I'll search first and then read the pages it returns, in this order:

1. **The traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word on Job 42, then Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com, then preceptaustin.org's Job 42 page.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), then Reformed and Baptist teachers (Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY, The Gospel Coalition), then Lutheran sources (1517.org, lcms.org). I'd focus on the verses most likely to differ:
   - v. 6: what Job's "repentance" means
   - vv. 7–8: in what sense Job "spoke accurately" about God
   - vv. 10–12: whether the doubled restoration is a pattern to expect
3. **Other views:**
   - netbible.org translator notes (for example on "retract" or "despise myself" in v. 6, and on v. 11)
   - bibleodyssey.org on how the epilogue relates to the poem
   - Catholic and Orthodox readings (newadvent.org, catholic.com, oca.org), including the longer ending of Job in the Greek Old Testament, if they mention it
   - what gotquestions.org and the other sites say about prosperity teaching using Job 42:10

Every point will have its URL, and I'll leave out anything I can't find.
